attributes.note: Illustrative graph based on the cited publications; it is not course material.

card.summary: With Graham Hitch, proposed a three-component model of working memory in 1974; later proposed the episodic buffer.

sections.heading: Why this person is here
sections.body: The graph links Baddeley to the original multicomponent model and to the later episodic-buffer proposal. The latter was introduced to account for phenomena the original model did not readily capture.

card.summary: Co-proposed the original three-component working memory model with Alan Baddeley in 1974.

sections.heading: Connection in this graph
sections.body: The authorship edge points to the model they proposed together. This card does not stand for every contribution in Hitch's research.

card.summary: Baddeley and Hitch's 1974 proposal described working memory as a system with three components.

sections.heading: Original proposal
sections.body: The model was proposed by Baddeley and Hitch in 1974. It provided an integrated account of findings from several lines of research, while later work identified phenomena the original version did not readily explain.

sections.heading: Later revision
sections.body: Baddeley proposed the episodic buffer as a fourth component in 2000. In this graph, that proposal is a separate node so the historical relation remains visible.

card.summary: A fourth component proposed in 2000 to temporarily hold integrated information in a multimodal code.

sections.heading: What it adds
sections.body: Baddeley described a limited-capacity system able to bind information from subsidiary systems and long-term memory into a unitary episodic representation.

sections.heading: Why the revision matters
sections.body: The proposal shifted attention toward how information is integrated across systems, rather than treating each subsidiary system in isolation.
